edition.alertText: CENTCOM launches Task Force Iron Gate — extends blockade to Iran's land borders and Caspian Sea routes; Trump tells CNN strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress on nuclear program and Hormuz reopening; four unexplained explosions rock Qeshm Island — IRNA reports impacts, cause unknown; Rubio casts doubt on Iran diplomacy at G7 Paris — calls Tehran's demands 'unrealistic'; Araghchi says no negotiations since midterm 'shock'; IRGC claims 3 tankers caught fire in Hormuz on 'unauthorized' route — mines and explosions reported; ADNOC-chartered Navig8 Messi catches fire off Khasab (2nd attack since Aug) — crew evacuated; US disables M/V Huda in Gulf of Oman for blockade breach; Houthi cruise missiles damage KAFD tower and Aramco building in Riyadh — Saudi coalition intercepts 2 missiles; drone strikes Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan — 70%+ of Kurdish region without power; Israel defense minister: 'mission not complete' on Iran; IRGC dismisses Iron Gate as 'wordplay'; Iran armed forces: US midterm defeat reflects failure against Iran; UAE rescues 22 from cargo ship fire in Sea of Oman; Brent falls to $97.67 (-0.65%); WTI $90.51 (-0.35%); gold ~$4,072 (-0.34%); US gas $4.02/gal (AAA); UKMTO/JMIC: IRGC drone overflights, surveillance, radio hailing persist in strait; vessel transits remain single-digit to low double-digit daily

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 255 as the United States escalated its economic pressure campaign with the launch of Task Force Iron Gate — a new CENTCOM unit based in Tampa, Florida, with approximately 20 personnel tasked with disrupting Iran's weapons shipments, sanctioned materials, and illicit revenue streams across land borders and through the Caspian Sea. Admiral Brad Cooper ordered the task force, extending the blockade well beyond its naval origins. Trump struck a notably more conciliatory tone over the weekend, telling CNN on Saturday evening that renewed strikes were 'highly unlikely' if there was progress in talks on Tehran's nuclear program and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, adding that it depends on whether Iran signs 'a very strong agreement.' Four unexplained explosions rocked Qeshm Island on Saturday evening, with IRNA confirming impacts at multiple locations; additional blasts were reported at Sirik, Jask, and Bandar Abbas, though Iranian officials gave no confirmed cause — coming days after the US struck the island's air defenses. Secretary of State Rubio arrived at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, where he cast doubt on Iran's diplomatic sincerity and called Tehran's conditions 'unrealistic.' Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi responded that there had been no negotiations since the 'shock' of the US midterm elections and that everything 'depends on the political rationality of Washington.' A drone struck the Khor Mor gas field in Iraqi Kurdistan on November 9, halting production and cutting power to more than 70% of the Kurdish region. Israel's Defense Minister Katz declared the 'mission is still not complete' on Iran. IRGC spokesman Mohebbi dismissed Task Force Iron Gate as 'merely a wordplay,' saying previous US naval, air, and land blockades had all failed. Iran's armed forces spokesman Shekarchi said the US midterm defeat reflected America's failure against Iran, while MP Ebrahim Azizi warned that midterm results would not change Iran's nuclear strategy.

Oil markets opened the week lower as Trump's conciliatory comments dampened fears of renewed US strikes. Brent crude fell 64 cents to $97.67/bbl (-0.65%) on Monday morning, with losses briefly exceeding $1 per barrel during the opening session before stabilizing. WTI eased to $90.51 (-0.35%). Despite the drop, prices remain elevated and supported by continued tanker attacks and IRGC claims of mine strikes in the strait. Gold traded at approximately $4,072/oz on Sunday, down 0.34% from $4,086 as the strong US jobs report (165K vs 65K expected) and elevated December Fed hike odds (77–80%) continued to weigh on haven demand. The 10-year Treasury yield held near 4.87%. Newcastle coal was little changed around $144–145/tonne. The US national average gasoline price fell to $4.02/gal (AAA, Nov 8), continuing its decline toward the sub-$4 level that GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan predicted could arrive within days. US diesel remained elevated at approximately $6.20/gal. VLCC rates held in the $420K–460K/day range for Arabian Gulf–China routes, with war-risk premiums stable amid continued attacks. The broader energy complex remained volatile, with Brent having plunged 16% in the prior week — its steepest weekly decline since 2020 — before partially stabilizing.

The maritime situation intensified over the weekend as Iran's IRGC claimed three tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday after transiting an 'unauthorized' route, with Fars news attributing two fires to naval mines and a third to an explosion. Earlier Saturday, the ADNOC-chartered tanker Navig8 Messi caught fire 8 nautical miles off Khasab, Oman — the vessel's second attack since August, when it was struck by IRGC drones — forcing crew evacuation with no injuries reported. UKMTO received a delayed report of a separate tanker struck by an unknown projectile during an outbound transit on Saturday, with the crew confirmed safe. The US disabled the St. Kitts-flagged cargo vessel M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday evening, firing precision munitions at its stern after the crew repeatedly attempted to breach the naval blockade. The UAE National Guard rescued 22 Arab nationals from a cargo ship fire in the Sea of Oman on Sunday. In a significant escalation, Houthi cruise missiles targeted Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District on Saturday, damaging a KAFD tower (Reuters) and causing a 'limited fire' at an Aramco building, with Saudi civil defence reporting injuries from intercepted missile debris. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two cruise missiles over Riyadh and destroyed a Houthi drone heading toward the eastern region, then struck Houthi missile launchers and a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa. UKMTO and the Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC) reported sustained IRGC activity in the strait including drone overflights, targeted surveillance of merchant shipping, and occasional VHF radio hailing. Vessel transits remain at single-digit to low-double-digit levels daily — roughly 65–70% below the pre-conflict baseline, with US-assisted transits averaging about 31 per day.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%. Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst).

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. India building two fertiliser futures — diversifying sources while lobbying for corridor (Diplomat Magazine). Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Hormuz crude recovery hides slower one for LNG, fertilizer, helium and aluminum — non-oil flows still near zero (Enterprise AM). Out of Hormuz energy shocks, the ingredients for a global food crisis intensify (PRNewswire/IFA).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas at €97.53/MWh (~$108.51), highest since 2022 energy crisis. Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war; group bars crew overnight stays in Israel through Nov 30. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.
